## Fix PHPStan errors in classes generated by `env-settings:make`

One bug, found by generating a settings class in a new Laravel 13 starter-kit app, whose `composer test` runs Larastan. No API change.

### Generated classes no longer fail `new.static`

Every factory in a generated class builds its instance with `new static(...)`, and the class is neither `final` nor has a final constructor. PHPStan cannot rule out a subclass whose constructor takes different arguments — `new static(...)` would then call it with the wrong ones — so it reported every factory, at every level, `0` included. A class straight out of v1.7.3:

```bash
php artisan env-settings:make AuthSettings --properties="domain:string,timeout:int"
```

```
 ------ ------------------------------------
  Line   app/Settings/AuthSettings.php
 ------ ------------------------------------
  18     Unsafe usage of new static().
         🪪  new.static
  26     Unsafe usage of new static().
         🪪  new.static
 ------ ------------------------------------

 [ERROR] Found 2 errors
```

Making the class `final` would silence it, but a generated class has to stay open: a local override extends it. The package's own override fixtures already had the answer, and v1.7.4 generates it:

```php
/**
 * Local overrides extend this class, so it is not final. They keep the same
 * constructor, which is what makes `new static()` safe.
 *
 * @phpstan-consistent-constructor
 */
class AuthSettings extends EnvironmentSettings
```

```
 [OK] No errors
```

Checked at levels 0, 7 and `max`, on classes generated plain, with `--sensitive` and with `--shared`.

The tag is a promise PHPStan holds you to. An override that redeclares the constructor with a different signature — the one case where an inherited factory's `new static(...)` really would break — is now reported:

```
  9      Method App\Settings\Overrides\AuthSettings::__construct() overrides
         method App\Settings\AuthSettings::__construct() but misses parameter
         #2 $timeout.
         🪪  parameter.missing
```

### Why it went unnoticed

The package's own PHPStan run covers `src` and `tests`. Its two non-final fixtures already carried `@phpstan-consistent-constructor`, and nothing analysed what the stub generates — so the check stayed green while every generated class failed it. A new test asserts the tag sits in the docblock attached to the generated class, and it fails against the old stub.

### Upgrading

No API change, and nothing changes for classes you already have: the stub only shapes classes generated from now on. If PHPStan reports `new.static` on an existing settings class — one generated before v1.7.4, or one written by hand — add the same docblock above its `class` line, or make the class `final` if no local override extends it. If the class has a local override that redeclares the constructor, PHPStan will then report that override, as shown above: fix the override, not the tag.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/HPWebdeveloper/laravel-env-settings/compare/v1.7.3...v1.7.4
